headline: A little more space.
intro: Thoughtful remote assistance for the calendar, inbox, projects, and details that compete for your attention. Build a working relationship around your priorities, your tools, and your way of doing business.
serviceTitle: Practical help. Personal to your work.
serviceIntro: Explore twelve ways an assistant can make your day more manageable. Each service has a clear scope, a useful output, and room for the preferences that make support feel like part of your team.
storyTitle: The best support makes the whole day feel different.
story: You should not have to hold every reminder, meeting detail, and open question in your head. A well-scoped assistant role gives those details a dependable home and brings the important decisions back to you.
footer: Dedicated remote assistants for executive organization, business administration, communication, and thoughtful day-to-day coordination.
contact: Tell us what would make your day easier.
prepare: The tasks that interrupt your focused work
Your calendar, communication, and approval preferences
A few examples of a useful handoff
pillars: Define what deserves immediate attention, what can wait, and which decisions should always come back to you.
Useful support keeps the purpose, preferences, and source information alongside each request.
Completed tasks come with the detail you need. Open questions come with a clear next step.

services.title: Executive Calendar Management
services.description: Protect executive time with controlled scheduling, complete context, and clear approval limits.
services.alt: A person marking a calendar beside a laptop and phone.
audience: Executives and leadership teams with recurring meeting requests, defined priorities, and an owner for exceptions.
services.problem: Calendar support fails when urgency, attendee purpose, time zones, travel buffers, and decision rights are hidden inside messages.
inputs: A released set of meeting requests
Current rules, examples, and required fields for the calendar

work: Triage meeting requests against published priorities

outputs: Handoff record with owner and due time
controls: Saved record compared with supporting evidence
